hybrid_pq_identity.description: Experimental hybrid Fabric identity mechanism: ECDSA X.509 membership and CA chain, a noncritical extension carrying the PQ algorithm and public key, and real liboqs-based peer transaction/endorsement signing and verification.
hybrid_pq_identity.orderer_binary_note: Patched to verify requests signed by PQ peer identities
hybrid_pq_identity.verification_dispatch: An X.509 certificate carrying experimental extension 1.3.6.1.3.9999.1 is imported as *sw.pqPublicKey before its ECDSA SPKI is considered. BCCSP dispatches that concrete key type only to pqPublicKeyVerifier, which initializes oqs.Signature with the extension algorithm and calls oqs.Signature.Verify. Import, initialization, or verification failure returns an error/false; there is no ECDSA verification fallback for the PQ key type.

runtime_verification_audit.status: complete; retained one-shot runtime traces validate actual liboqs PQ verification on the orderer and peers in both organizations for all three PQ configurations
runtime_verification_audit.trace_control: FABRIC_PQ_VERIFY_TRACE=1 enables one INFO trace per algorithm/result pair per process; Caliper run_e1.sh rejects this setting so trace logging cannot perturb performance runs
runtime_verification_audit.regression_test: bccsp/sw TestPQVerifierDispatchRejectsClassicalFallback covers ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s-simple
runtime_verification_audit.regression_interpretation: For every supported PQ algorithm, a valid PQ signature verifies, a tampered PQ signature is rejected, and an ECDSA signature presented to the PQ public key is rejected by the concrete PQ verifier without classical fallback.

caliper.fixed_profile_status: unchanged common-profile comparison for all four configurations
caliper.endorsement_timing_boundary: Wall-clock interval immediately before proposal.endorse() until that promise resolves; it excludes proposal construction and the later submit/commit interval.
caliper.commit_timing_boundary: Post-endorsement submit-to-commit-status wall-clock interval: starts immediately before transaction.submit(), after proposal.endorse() resolves; includes client transaction-envelope signing, Gateway Submit RPC and any wait until orderer acknowledgement, commit-status request signing/RPC, ordering/block-cut wait (including BatchTimeout when active), validation/ledger commit, and client/event-loop waiting within those awaited calls; ends when submittedTransaction.getStatus() resolves. It excludes endorsement and Caliper scheduling/queueing before this connector call.
caliper.commit_timing_limitation: The single wall-clock value does not decompose client-side async/RPC waiting, orderer acceptance, block-cut waiting, validation, ledger commit, and status delivery.
caliper.end_to_end_timing_boundary: immediately before proposal.endorse() through successful commit status or the caught failure

sustainability.successful_throughput_definition: Caliper success count divided by the configured 60-second round duration; Caliper displayed throughput is retained but is not used because it can include failed completions.
sustainability.latency_population: successful end-to-end transaction samples ordered by monotonic request-start offset
sustainability.beginning_window: start offsets in [0,12000) ms, the first 20 percent of a 60-second round
sustainability.ending_window: start offsets in [48000,60000) ms, the last 20 percent of a 60-second round
sustainability.final_sphincs_rule: highest tested low-rate sweep point passing all three criteria

The legacy raw summary grouped unavailable with invalid; the analyzer reports valid=0, invalid=0, unavailable=1201 without modifying raw evidence.

latency_professor_review.final_latency_population: Clean 200-TPS common-profile rows for ECDSA, ML-DSA-44, and ML-DSA-65; clean 50-TPS rows are supporting; SPHINCS+ rows are saturation-only.

clean_cross_configuration_review.cadence_interpretation: The monotonic 200-TPS height deltas (60, 180, 238 blocks) are consistent with larger serialized transactions producing more size-driven cuts plus periodic residual cuts, while ECDSA's 60 blocks in 120 seconds are consistent with BatchTimeout=2s. Height deltas alone do not identify each block's cut trigger, so this is strongly supported rather than causal proof.

block_utilisation.definition: mean(actual ordinary-transaction block bytes) / effective PreferredMaxBytes
block_utilisation.scientific_condition: Exclude genesis/config/other blocks; retain terminal ordinary partial blocks. The observed steady-state population must not be BatchTimeout-driven.
block_utilisation.diagnostic_rate_status: 300 TPS was a block-filling probe only. Its block evidence is accepted for block utilisation; Gateway concurrency-limit failures make the run invalid for final latency or tps_sustained.
block_utilisation.observed_closure: Documented empirical observation: blocks 17-47 each contain MaxMessageCount=500 ordinary transactions, demonstrating steady-state count-limit closure rather than BatchTimeout closure. Block 48 is a terminal 386-transaction ordinary block retained in the accepted population.

working_result.population_rule: Exclude genesis/config/other blocks and retain every ordinary transaction block in the measured interval, including the terminal partial block.

full_500_transaction_block_diagnostic_co.status: diagnostic comparison only; does not replace the accepted boundary-inclusive result

block_utilisation.transaction_size_method: For each fetched serialized common.Block, decode protobuf Block.Data.Data[i] as the exact common.Envelope bytes. Record len(Data[i]), SHA-256, transaction ID, validation code, and endorsement count per transaction. tx_bytes_mean is the arithmetic mean of these exact envelope lengths for endorser transactions in accepted ordinary blocks; it is never estimated as block bytes divided by transaction count.
block_utilisation.tx_bytes_status: ECDSA, ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and SPHINCS+ all have accepted exact-envelope and empirical endorsement evidence. The timeout-driven 50-TPS block populations remain diagnostic-only; the older ECDSA block-filling CSV remains the separate accepted block-utilisation source.
